name: Seo Ha-eun
bio: Seo Ha-eun is a radio host based in Gyeongju, South Korea, where she presents a weekday afternoon program of listener letters, local weather notes, and requested music. She began in community broadcasting while studying Korean literature, and is known for segments in which older residents describe changes to their neighborhoods over the decades.

name: Meseret Alemayehu Gebre
bio: Meseret Alemayehu Gebre is a museum curator based in Addis Ababa, where she oversees collections of textiles, manuscripts, and everyday objects drawn from communities across the Ethiopian highlands. She trained in art history and conservation before moving into exhibition work, and she regularly writes bilingual catalogue entries in Amharic and English for visiting researchers and school groups.

name: Imane Bel Khadir
bio: Imane Bel Khadir is a museum curator based in Marrakesh, Morocco, where she specializes in textiles and decorative metalwork from the surrounding plains and mountain valleys. She studied art history and conservation before returning to the city to organize permanent collections and seasonal exhibitions, and she frequently writes bilingual catalogue notes in Arabic and French.

name: Anjali Vadakkedath Nair
bio: Anjali Vadakkedath Nair is a documentary photographer born in Thrissur, Kerala, who works primarily in black-and-white portraiture of coastal and agricultural communities. She studied visual communication in Kochi and has since divided her time between fieldwork along the backwaters and teaching short darkroom workshops.

name: Oyunbileg Dashnyam
bio: Oyunbileg Dashnyam is a textile designer based in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, known for work that adapts traditional felting and weaving techniques to contemporary interior fabrics. She trained in applied arts before spending several years in workshop production, and she now divides her time between studio design work and teaching short courses on dyeing and pattern drafting.

name: Nuala Ferriter
bio: Nuala Ferriter is a sculptor based in Galway, Ireland, known for carved limestone and cast bronze works that reference coastal field walls and fishing gear. She trained in Ireland and later worked from a converted boat shed on the Connemara coast, exhibiting mainly in regional galleries and public commissions.

name: Kanyarat Thepsiri
bio: Kanyarat Thepsiri is a documentary photographer born and raised in Chiang Mai, Thailand, where she first learned darkroom printing from a neighbor who repaired cameras. Her work focuses on artisan workshops, seasonal markets, and river landscapes across northern Thailand, and she has taught introductory photography courses in Thai and English.

name: Nino Dzamashvili
bio: Nino Dzamashvili is a jazz composer and pianist born in Tbilisi, Georgia, who began formal music study as a child before turning to improvised idioms in her twenties. Her work is often described as combining modal jazz writing with the layered vocal traditions of the Caucasus, and she has led small ensembles in Georgia and elsewhere in Europe since the early 2010s.

name: Marilene Bastos Quirino
bio: Marilene Bastos Quirino is a landscape architect born in Salvador, Bahia, who studied architecture and urbanism before specializing in public open spaces and coastal vegetation. Her work focuses on shaded plazas, rainwater gardens, and the use of native caatinga and Atlantic Forest species in municipal parks across the Recôncavo.

name: Rukia Mzee Khamis
bio: Rukia Mzee Khamis is a sculptor based in Stone Town, Zanzibar, who works primarily in carved hardwood, coral rag, and cast brass. Trained first through an informal apprenticeship with neighborhood door-carvers and later in a coastal crafts program, she is known for large standing forms that adapt motifs from local joinery and boatbuilding.

name: Temitope Adebayo-Ilesanmi
bio: Temitope Adebayo-Ilesanmi is a documentary filmmaker based in Lagos, Nigeria, known for observational films about ferry commuters, market traders, and neighbourhood archivists along the city's waterfront. She studied mass communication before working as a sound recordist, and now divides her time between directing, teaching short workshops, and restoring old regional footage.

name: Soukaina Talmoudi Regragui
bio: Soukaina Talmoudi Regragui is a chef and food writer based in Marrakesh, Morocco, where she trained in family kitchens before completing a culinary apprenticeship in Casablanca. She writes a long-running column on regional home cooking in Darija and French, and has published two recipe collections documenting dishes from the plains and foothills around the city.

name: Kertu Vainola
bio: Kertu Vainola is an investigative journalist based in Tartu, Estonia, who reports mainly on municipal procurement, housing records, and environmental permitting in the country's southern counties. She studied semiotics and media before turning to document-driven reporting, and she frequently publishes in both Estonian and English.

name: Imogen Braddock
bio: Imogen Braddock is a landscape architect based in Hobart, Tasmania, whose practice focuses on riverside public spaces and the rehabilitation of former orchard land. She trained in environmental design before spending several years on coastal walkway and stormwater planting projects across southern Tasmania.

name: Salma Nassor Vuai
bio: Salma Nassor Vuai is a jazz composer and pianist from Stone Town on the island of Unguja, Zanzibar, whose work blends modern jazz harmony with coastal Swahili song forms. She began as an accompanist for taarab ensembles before turning to composition, and now writes for small jazz groups, film, and school music programs across the archipelago.

name: Ketevan Meparishvili
bio: Ketevan Meparishvili is a ceramic artist based in Tbilisi, Georgia, known for hand-built stoneware vessels that adapt the profiles of traditional wine jars to contemporary tableware. She trained in applied arts in the city, apprenticed with rural potters in eastern Georgia, and now teaches occasional wheel-throwing workshops while maintaining a small studio kiln.

name: Maëlle Thibodeau-Groulx
bio: Maëlle Thibodeau-Groulx is a chef and food writer born in Trois-Rivières and based in Montréal, where she trained in restaurant kitchens before turning to writing about regional cooking. She publishes essays and recipe columns in French and English, focusing on seasonal produce, dairy traditions, and the maple harvest of the Québec countryside.

name: Rhodora Malinao Panisales
bio: Rhodora Malinao Panisales is a radio host based in Cagayan de Oro, Mindanao, where she presents a weekday morning program that mixes community announcements, listener call-ins, and local music. She began in broadcasting as a student volunteer producing Cebuano-language public service segments, and she later worked as a news reader before moving to hosting.

name: Parisa Mostowfi Golshani
bio: Parisa Mostowfi Golshani is a museum curator based in Isfahan, Iran, who specializes in regional decorative arts and the documentation of historic tilework. She studied art history and conservation before taking up curatorial work, and she has organized exhibitions pairing archival photographs with objects from workshop traditions of the surrounding province.

name: Rosalba Jiménez Matadamas
bio: Rosalba Jiménez Matadamas is a textile designer from the Central Valleys of Oaxaca, Mexico, who works primarily with backstrap and pedal looms and natural dyes derived from local plants and insects. She trained in graphic design in the city of Oaxaca de Juárez before returning to her family's weaving workshop, where she now develops contemporary garment collections alongside documentation of regional pattern vocabularies.

name: Ileana Morărescu Bâlc
bio: Ileana Morărescu Bâlc is a landscape architect based in Cluj-Napoca, where she works on public squares, riverside walkways, and courtyard gardens in older parts of the city. Trained in horticulture before turning to design, she is known for planting schemes that rely on meadow species found in the surrounding Transylvanian hills.

name: Dandara Sampaio Ferraz
bio: Dandara Sampaio Ferraz is a documentary filmmaker born in Salvador, Bahia, who studied audiovisual communication before working as a sound assistant on regional film crews. Her documentaries focus on fishing communities, rural festivals, and oral storytelling traditions across the Recôncavo and the Bahian interior.

name: Amaranta Sosa Yescas
bio: Amaranta Sosa Yescas is a radio host based in Oaxaca de Juárez who presents a weekday morning program combining regional music, listener call-ins, and interviews with artisans and farmers. She began in community broadcasting in the Valles Centrales and later trained younger presenters in bilingual Spanish and Zapotec programming.

name: Fenella Marchbank
bio: Fenella Marchbank is a chef and food writer based in Hobart, Tasmania, known for menus built around cool-climate produce from the Derwent Valley and the island's east coast. After training in restaurant kitchens in Launceston, she began writing a regular column on Tasmanian seasonal cooking and later published a collection of essays and recipes on southern Australian coastal foodways.

name: Mariela Ancalef Zúñiga
bio: Mariela Ancalef Zúñiga is a documentary filmmaker based in the Argentine province of Chubut, known for observational films about wool-shearing routes, coastal fishing families, and rural schools across the Patagonian steppe. She works primarily in Spanish, often incorporating Mapudungun testimony, and has taught short workshops on field sound recording for community media groups.

name: Nicandro Pacheco Chagoya
bio: Nicandro Pacheco Chagoya is a poet from the Sierra Norte of Oaxaca, Mexico, who writes in Spanish and Zapotec and is known for short lyric sequences about mountain agriculture and seasonal migration. He began publishing in regional literary magazines in his late twenties and has since taught community writing workshops in several Oaxacan towns.

name: Léandre Cormier-Baril
bio: Léandre Cormier-Baril is a ceramic artist based in Quebec, Canada, known for stoneware vessels glazed in muted river tones drawn from the Saint-Laurent valley. Raised in a francophone household and trained in both pottery and art history, he divides his time between studio production, kiln experiments, and teaching seasonal workshops.

name: Behnaz Rahmatian Khorasgani
bio: Behnaz Rahmatian Khorasgani is a chef and food writer based in Isfahan, Iran, known for documenting household cooking traditions of the central Iranian plateau. She trained in a family catering kitchen before turning to writing, and publishes recipe essays in Persian and English on regional stews, breads, and confections.

name: Agata Lo Verso Pennisi
bio: Agata Lo Verso Pennisi is a theater director from Sicily, Italy, who trained in dramaturgy in Palermo before working with touring companies across the island. Her productions often adapt Sicilian oral storytelling traditions for contemporary stages, and she has led workshops for young performers in Catania and Siracusa.

name: Itzel Guendulain Zárate
bio: Itzel Guendulain Zárate is a museum curator based in Oaxaca de Juárez, where she specializes in textile collections and community-held archives from the Central Valleys. She studied art history and museum documentation before spending most of her career organizing exhibitions that pair contemporary work with older regional craft traditions.

name: Devika Thottathil Menon
bio: Devika Thottathil Menon is a jazz composer born in Thrissur, Kerala, who studied piano and Carnatic vocal music before turning to ensemble writing. She is known for arrangements that pair modal jazz harmony with Malayalam-language lyrics and percussion patterns drawn from temple festival traditions.

name: Folasade Oyinlola Akintayo
bio: Folasade Oyinlola Akintayo is a folk musician from Lagos, Nigeria, known for performing Yoruba praise songs accompanied by talking drum and thumb piano. She began singing at neighbourhood gatherings in her teens and later worked as a music teacher while touring coastal towns in the south-west of the country.

name: Océane Bergevin Turcotte
bio: Océane Bergevin Turcotte is a Québécois photographer based in Montréal, known for large-format landscape studies of the Laurentians and winter light along the St. Lawrence. She trained in visual arts in Sherbrooke, works primarily in French, and has taught seasonal darkroom workshops for community arts centres in the Saguenay region.

name: Selamawit Terefe Bogale
bio: Selamawit Terefe Bogale is an investigative journalist based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, where she reports on public procurement, municipal budgets, and land administration records. She studied journalism and statistics before spending a decade with regional newspapers, and she publishes in both Amharic and English.

name: Maricarmen Robledo Alcaraz
bio: Maricarmen Robledo Alcaraz is a ceramic artist born in Seville, in the southern Spanish region of Andalusia, where she trained in tin-glazed tilework before opening a small studio of her own. Her work combines traditional Andalusian glazing methods with large-format panels commissioned for courtyards, libraries, and municipal buildings across the region.

name: Nayra Ccorimanya Huarcaya
bio: Nayra Ccorimanya Huarcaya is a landscape architect based in Cusco, Peru, whose work focuses on terraced hillside parks, native plant corridors, and public stairways in steep neighborhoods. She trained in architecture and soil conservation before specializing in the restoration of Andean agricultural terraces and the design of water-sensitive plazas for small highland towns.

name: Enkhjargal Tsogtbaatar
bio: Enkhjargal Tsogtbaatar is a jazz composer and arranger based in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, known for scoring small ensembles that place piano alongside traditional Mongolian string instruments. She studied music theory and conducting in the capital before spending several years leading rehearsal workshops and writing for radio broadcasts and chamber-jazz programs.

name: Elvira Ccahuana Huarancca
bio: Elvira Ccahuana Huarancca is a museum curator based in Cusco, Peru, where she specializes in Andean textile collections and colonial-era ceramics. She studied art history and archaeology at a regional university before spending several years cataloguing community heritage holdings in the Sacred Valley.

name: Odile Charbonneau Fréchette
bio: Odile Charbonneau Fréchette is a jazz composer and pianist from Quebec, Canada, known for ensemble works that draw on francophone folk song forms. She studied classical piano before turning to composition, and has written for small jazz groups, chamber orchestras, and documentary film scores.

name: Nawin Suthakul
bio: Nawin Suthakul is a theater director based in Chiang Mai, Thailand, whose productions combine spoken drama with Lanna shadow-puppet and masked dance traditions. After studying dramatic arts in Bangkok, he returned north to work with community troupes in the Ping River valley and to teach staging workshops for student performers.

name: Candela Berrocal Ojeda
bio: Candela Berrocal Ojeda is a choreographer based in Seville, Andalusia, whose work combines flamenco vocabulary with contemporary stage movement. She trained in classical Spanish dance before touring southern Spain as a rehearsal director and later teaching seasonal workshops for regional dance students.

name: Mahasti Forouzandeh Sepahani
bio: Mahasti Forouzandeh Sepahani is a poet from Isfahan, Iran, known for short lyric sequences written in Persian that draw on the rhythms of everyday neighborhood life. She began publishing in regional literary magazines in her twenties and has since taken part in provincial poetry gatherings and translation workshops.

name: Perla Mendieta Ramales
bio: Perla Mendieta Ramales is a documentary filmmaker born in the city of Oaxaca de Juárez and raised partly in a Zapotec-speaking town in the Tlacolula valley. She works mainly in Spanish and Zapotec, making observational films about rural water management, weaving households, and seasonal migration in southern Mexico.

name: Sunniva Aardal Fjeldstad
bio: Sunniva Aardal Fjeldstad is a folk musician from Bergen, Norway, known for performing traditional dance tunes and ballads on the Hardanger fiddle. She grew up in a coastal village in the surrounding Vestland region and later settled in the city, where she teaches and arranges regional song repertoire.

name: Sylvain Lapointe Desrochers
bio: Sylvain Lapointe Desrochers is a radio host from Quebec, Canada, known for morning talk programming that blends regional news with conversations about local music. He studied communications before moving into broadcasting, and he presents primarily in French while occasionally producing bilingual segments for listeners outside the province.

name: Nanae Tsurumaki
bio: Nanae Tsurumaki is a folk musician from Hokkaido, Japan, known for arranging northern fishing and harvest songs for voice and plucked strings. She began performing at regional community halls in her twenties and later taught seasonal song repertoire to amateur choirs across the island.

name: Ryu Do-kyung
bio: Ryu Do-kyung is an investigative journalist from Gyeongju, in the Gyeongsangbuk-do province of South Korea, who reports mainly on regional development spending and heritage site management. After studying Korean literature and later completing a graduate program in public records research, she spent a decade writing long-form pieces for provincial news outlets before turning to freelance investigative work.

name: Kehinde Bamidele Oshoniyi
bio: Kehinde Bamidele Oshoniyi is a museum curator based in Lagos, Nigeria, who specializes in twentieth-century textile design and photographic archives. He studied art history and conservation before taking up curatorial work, and he frequently organizes exhibitions that pair historical objects with commentary from contemporary artisans.

name: Ofelia Lavariega Cortés
bio: Ofelia Lavariega Cortés is a radio host from Oaxaca de Juárez, Mexico, who presents a midday cultural magazine program in Spanish and Zapotec. She began her career recording community announcements for a small station in the Sierra Norte before moving to the state capital, where she also trains volunteer broadcasters from rural municipalities.

name: Rómulo Quispe Ttito
bio: Rómulo Quispe Ttito is a photographer born and raised in Cusco, Peru, where he grew up speaking both Quechua and Spanish. He is known for documentary series on highland market towns and terraced farmland in the surrounding Andean valleys, work he has exhibited locally and published in regional photography anthologies.

name: Tinatin Khvedeliani
bio: Tinatin Khvedeliani is a folk musician based in Tbilisi who performs traditional vocal polyphony and accompanies herself on the panduri. She grew up in a family of highland singers, studied choral arrangement in the capital, and later began teaching regional singing styles to amateur ensembles.

name: Véronique Dansereau Pelletier
bio: Véronique Dansereau Pelletier is a radio host based in Montréal who presents a weekday midday program of interviews and listener call-ins in French. She began her career producing community broadcasts in the Outaouais region before moving to a Québécois talk network, where she has also written a column on francophone music.

name: Sorcha Mulqueen
bio: Sorcha Mulqueen is a ceramic artist based in Galway, on Ireland's west coast, who works primarily in hand-built stoneware and locally sourced slips. She trained in craft and design before setting up a small studio where she also teaches evening wheel-throwing classes in English and Irish.

name: Rocío Almagro Trujillo
bio: Rocío Almagro Trujillo is a radio host from Seville, in the Andalusian region of southern Spain, known for daytime cultural programmes broadcast in Spanish. She studied audiovisual communication before working as a producer for regional stations along the Guadalquivir valley.

name: Nuria Zamorano Peñalver
bio: Nuria Zamorano Peñalver is a poet from Granada, in the Andalusian region of southern Spain, who writes primarily in Spanish and publishes short lyric collections. She studied philology before working as a literary translator, and her poems frequently draw on the landscapes and rural vocabulary of the Guadalquivir valley.

name: Editha Tampus Manlangit
bio: Editha Tampus Manlangit is a documentary and portrait photographer based in Davao City, on the southern Philippine island of Mindanao, where she has worked since the early 2000s. Her long-running projects focus on coastal fishing households, upland weaving traditions, and the everyday life of Cebuano- and Maguindanaon-speaking communities, and her prints have circulated through regional exhibitions and small photo journals.

name: Róisín Concannon
bio: Róisín Concannon is a radio host based in Galway, Ireland, known for presenting a weekday mid-morning programme that mixes local news interviews with traditional and contemporary music. Raised in a bilingual household on the edge of the Connemara Gaeltacht, she studied media and Irish-language broadcasting before moving into full-time presenting work in her mid-twenties.

name: Deirbhile Lohan
bio: Deirbhile Lohan is a textile designer based in Galway, Ireland, whose work centres on handwoven wool cloth and naturally dyed linen. Raised in a coastal village west of the city, she trained in woven textiles before establishing a small studio practice that combines floor-loom weaving with contemporary colour research.

name: Rosalie Beauchemin Pilon
bio: Rosalie Beauchemin Pilon is an investigative journalist from Trois-Rivières, Quebec, who reports in French and English on municipal contracting and regional land use. After studying literature at a public cégep and later completing a graduate certificate in documentary research, she spent a decade with small riverside weeklies before moving to longer-form accountability reporting.

name: Anca Trifoiu Berbecaru
bio: Anca Trifoiu Berbecaru is a novelist from Cluj-Napoca, in the Transylvania region of Romania, known for quiet family sagas set in small Carpathian market towns. She writes primarily in Romanian, occasionally incorporating Hungarian and Saxon dialect phrases drawn from the multilingual communities of her childhood.

name: Iracema Nogueira Vilasboas
bio: Iracema Nogueira Vilasboas is a poet from Salvador, Bahia, who writes in Portuguese and is known for short lyric sequences about coastal towns of the Recôncavo. She studied literature before working as a librarian, and has published several collections along with translations of regional folk verse.

name: Marisol Yupanqui Callañaupa
bio: Marisol Yupanqui Callañaupa is a landscape architect based in Cusco, Peru, whose work focuses on public plazas, riverside walkways, and the restoration of terraced slopes on the city's outskirts. Raised in a Quechua-speaking household in the Sacred Valley, she often writes about pairing traditional Andean water channels with contemporary park design.

name: Pimchanok Wongdara
bio: Pimchanok Wongdara is a textile designer based in Chiang Mai, Thailand, whose work centers on handwoven cotton and naturally dyed cloth produced with weavers in the surrounding northern valleys. She studied applied arts before turning to independent practice, and she also teaches short workshops on loom setup and plant-based dyeing for local craft groups.

name: Eimear Naughton
bio: Eimear Naughton is a landscape and documentary photographer based in Galway, on Ireland's western seaboard, where she has worked since completing a diploma in visual media. Her projects focus on coastal communities, seasonal light, and the changing shoreline of the Connacht coast, and her prints have been shown in regional group exhibitions.

name: Tamsin Weatherall
bio: Tamsin Weatherall is a contemporary dance choreographer born in Hobart, Tasmania, who trained in Launceston before developing work for small ensembles across southern Australia. Her pieces are often staged in converted warehouses and coastal halls, and she has taught movement workshops for regional community groups since the early 2010s.

name: Gaétan Mireault Lacoursière
bio: Gaétan Mireault Lacoursière is a folk musician from the Mauricie region of Quebec, Canada, known for fiddle tunes and call-and-response songs sung in French. He learned much of his repertoire from family kitchen gatherings before performing at regional festivals and recording several albums of traditional québécois dance music.

name: Maarika Pärnsalu
bio: Maarika Pärnsalu is a poet based in Tartu, Estonia, who writes in Estonian with occasional passages in the South Estonian Võro variety. Her collections are known for quiet riverside imagery drawn from walks along the Emajõgi and for short cycles about winter light in Tartumaa.

name: Lualhati Bacayo Sumagaysay
bio: Lualhati Bacayo Sumagaysay is a poet from Davao City in southern Mindanao who writes primarily in Cebuano and Filipino, with occasional English translations of her own work. Her collections draw on coastal barangay life, upland agricultural seasons, and oral storytelling traditions she encountered while teaching literature in provincial secondary schools.

name: Jandira Vasconcelos Pitanga
bio: Jandira Vasconcelos Pitanga is a radio host from Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, known for a weekday morning program mixing regional music with listener call-ins. She studied communication in her home state and previously worked as a newsroom assistant in the Recôncavo before moving into live broadcasting.

name: Haruna Kadowaki
bio: Haruna Kadowaki is a folk musician from Hokkaido, Japan, known for performing regional work songs and fishing ballads on a tonkori and a five-string banjo. She began playing at community festivals in her coastal hometown and later toured small venues across northern Japan, often presenting lyrics in both standard Japanese and local dialect.

name: Fidelina Aquino Chiñas
bio: Fidelina Aquino Chiñas is a chef and food writer from the Central Valleys of Oaxaca, Mexico, known for documenting home cooking traditions in Spanish and Zapotec. She trained in a family kitchen before opening a small dining room in Oaxaca de Juárez and began publishing recipe essays and regional ingredient guides in the early 2010s.

name: Merrin Quayle
bio: Merrin Quayle is a folk musician from Tasmania, Australia, who grew up in the Huon Valley south of Hobart and began performing at regional community halls as a teenager. Their repertoire centres on fiddle and button accordion arrangements of colonial-era ballads collected across the island, often performed at bush dances and small winter festivals.

name: Teódula Nolasco Gopar
bio: Teódula Nolasco Gopar is a folk musician from a Zapotec-speaking town in the Tlacolula valley of Oaxaca, Mexico, known for singing traditional sones and jarabes accompanied by guitar and harp. She learned the repertoire from village wind-band and dance traditions, and has spent much of her career teaching regional song forms to younger performers in the Sierra Norte and the Valles Centrales.

name: Munkhzul Baasandorj
bio: Munkhzul Baasandorj is a photographer based in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, known for documentary series on winter light in the city's outer districts. She studied visual arts locally before working for regional magazines, and she often photographs herding families on the surrounding steppe during seasonal migrations.

name: Clémence Bouthillier Rancourt
bio: Clémence Bouthillier Rancourt is a Québécois photographer known for large-format landscape work along the Saint Lawrence and for portrait series documenting rural francophone communities. Raised in the Saguenay region and later based in Montréal, she teaches seasonal darkroom workshops and publishes bilingual photo essays.

name: Nam Ji Won
bio: Nam Ji Won is a jazz composer from Gyeongju, South Korea, who writes for small ensembles that pair piano with traditional Korean string instruments. He began arranging music while studying composition in the city and has since focused on pieces inspired by the landscapes and historical sites of the surrounding region.

name: Sigrun Mjelde Haukås
bio: Sigrun Mjelde Haukås is a jazz composer who grew up in the Nordnes district of Bergen, Norway, and began writing for small ensembles while studying piano and arranging in the city. Her work is often described as drawing on Norwegian folk melody and the coastal weather of Vestland, and she has written for both quintets and chamber-sized string groups.

name: Bronwyn Callister
bio: Bronwyn Callister is a ceramic artist based in southern Tasmania, Australia, known for hand-built stoneware vessels finished with ash and mineral glazes. Raised in a family of orchardists in the Huon Valley, she trained in studio ceramics in Hobart before establishing a small kiln workshop that she also uses for weekend teaching.

name: Yohannes Tadesse Woldemariam
bio: Yohannes Tadesse Woldemariam is a sculptor based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, known for welded metal and carved stone figures that draw on Ge'ez manuscript ornament. He trained in fine art in the capital before teaching evening studio courses and exhibiting in group shows across the highlands.

name: Zuhura Mwinyi Juma
bio: Zuhura Mwinyi Juma is a choreographer from Stone Town on Unguja island in Zanzibar, Tanzania, known for staging ensemble works that pair coastal ngoma movement vocabulary with contemporary dance structures. She trained first in community dance groups before studying performance arts on the mainland, and later returned to the archipelago to teach workshops and develop pieces with Swahili-language musicians.

name: Thidarat Chaiyasaeng
bio: Thidarat Chaiyasaeng is a poet based in Chiang Mai, Thailand, whose short lyric sequences draw on the rhythms of spoken Kham Mueang and the seasonal life of the northern highlands. She studied Thai literature locally before publishing several small-press collections and taking part in regional reading circles along the Ping River.

name: Soledad Ixtepan Marroquín
bio: Soledad Ixtepan Marroquín is a ceramic artist from the Valles Centrales of Oaxaca, Mexico, who works primarily in burnished blackware and unglazed earthenware. She learned hand-building and pit-firing techniques from family workshops in her hometown before developing a studio practice that combines domestic vessel forms with contemporary sculptural pieces.

name: Tomoharu Ebisawa
bio: Tomoharu Ebisawa is a sculptor based in the coastal outskirts of Otaru, Hokkaido, who works primarily in weathered driftwood, basalt, and cast bronze. Trained first as a furniture maker, he became known for large outdoor pieces installed in northern parks, where he treats snowfall and sea wind as part of each work's finished surface.

name: Nohemí Sarabia Toledo
bio: Nohemí Sarabia Toledo is a poet from Oaxaca, Mexico, who writes in Spanish and Zapotec and grew up between the Istmo lowlands and the highland villages of the Sierra Norte. Her published collections draw on oral storytelling, market speech, and the bilingual rhythms of everyday Oaxacan life.

name: Sreelakshmi Puthenveettil Warrier
bio: Sreelakshmi Puthenveettil Warrier is a novelist from Kerala, India, who writes in Malayalam and publishes occasional self-translations in English. Raised in a family of schoolteachers near the backwaters of Alappuzha, she is known for domestic novels set in small trading towns along the Kerala coast.

name: Teodelina Bahamonde Cárcamo
bio: Teodelina Bahamonde Cárcamo is an Argentine poet raised in a wool-trading town on the windswept meseta of Chubut Province, where she began writing verse while working as a rural schoolteacher. Her collections draw on Patagonian landscape imagery and on Mapudungun place names, and she has edited several regional anthologies of contemporary verse.

name: Tiberiu Pîrvulescu Mărginean
bio: Tiberiu Pîrvulescu Mărginean is a documentary filmmaker based in Cluj-Napoca who works primarily in Romanian and Hungarian, often with subtitled releases for festival audiences abroad. His films focus on rural craft traditions, seasonal migration, and the changing landscapes of villages in the Apuseni Mountains.

name: Vakhtang Nadiradze
bio: Vakhtang Nadiradze is a landscape architect based in Tbilisi, Georgia, whose work focuses on terraced hillside gardens, riverside promenades, and drought-tolerant planting suited to the Caucasus climate. Trained in architecture and horticulture, he writes in Georgian and Russian on the restoration of courtyard greenery in older districts of the city.

name: Calogero Militello Sgroi
bio: Calogero Militello Sgroi is a choreographer born in Catania, Sicily, who trained in contemporary dance in Palermo before returning to the eastern coast to teach. His work is often described as pairing folk step patterns from inland Sicilian villages with minimalist stage design, and he lectures occasionally on movement notation in Italian and Sicilian.

name: Ligaya Tagolimot Cabahug
bio: Ligaya Tagolimot Cabahug is a chef and food writer from Davao City in Mindanao, Philippines, who trained in small family kitchens along the Davao Gulf before opening her own dining room. She writes in Cebuano and English about regional cooking, documenting recipes for kinilaw, palapa, and durian sweets gathered from home cooks across the island.

name: Meenakshi Kunnathoor Pillai
bio: Meenakshi Kunnathoor Pillai is a ceramic artist based in Kozhikode, Kerala, who works primarily in wheel-thrown stoneware fired with locally sourced clay bodies. She learned pottery from village artisans in her Malayalam-speaking hometown before developing a studio practice centred on tableware and architectural tile panels.

name: Caoilfhionn Tiernan
bio: Caoilfhionn Tiernan is a theater director based in Galway, Ireland, known for staging bilingual productions that move between English and Irish. She began her career assisting on touring shows in small Connemara venues before establishing her own rehearsal collective in the city.

name: Mizuki Shiratori
bio: Mizuki Shiratori is a chef and food writer born in Otaru, Hokkaido, who trained in seafood cookery along the Ishikari coast before opening a small seasonal kitchen in Sapporo. She writes a monthly column in Japanese on northern produce, dairy, and preserved foods, and has published two recipe collections aimed at home cooks.

name: Altantsetseg Jargalsaikhan
bio: Altantsetseg Jargalsaikhan is a poet based in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, who writes primarily in Mongolian and occasionally translates her own work into English. Raised in a family of herders who resettled in the capital, she is known for short lyric sequences that set steppe imagery against the routines of modern city life.

name: Amancay Painequeo Zalazar
bio: Amancay Painequeo Zalazar is a textile designer based in the Chubut valley of Argentine Patagonia, where she develops woven goods that adapt highland loom techniques to contemporary interiors. Trained in applied arts in Neuquén, she works mainly with guanaco and merino fibers and has taught seasonal dyeing workshops for rural weaving cooperatives across the steppe.

name: Aoibheann Mannion
bio: Aoibheann Mannion is a museum curator based in Galway, Ireland, who specialises in coastal craft traditions and domestic textiles of the western seaboard. She trained in art history and archival practice before taking up curatorial work, and she regularly prepares bilingual exhibition labels in English and Irish for visiting school groups.

name: Marivic Ompad Dalumpines
bio: Marivic Ompad Dalumpines is a novelist from the coastal lowlands of northern Mindanao, Philippines, who writes chiefly in Cebuano with self-translations into Filipino and English. Her long fiction is known for multigenerational family narratives set among fishing and copra-trading communities, and she has taught creative writing workshops for regional student groups.

name: Hwang Mi Rae
bio: Hwang Mi Rae is an investigative journalist based in Gyeongju, South Korea, who reports on municipal contracting, heritage-site management, and regional transit funding. She began her career writing for a small weekly in Gyeongsangbuk-do before moving into long-form accountability reporting, and she frequently lectures on public-records research for Korean-language newsrooms.

name: Keisuke Motomiya
bio: Keisuke Motomiya is a sculptor based in Sapporo, Hokkaido, who works primarily in carved birch, basalt, and cast bronze at a converted dairy shed outside the city. Trained in northern Japan and later in stone workshops abroad, he is known for outdoor pieces designed to change appearance under heavy seasonal snowfall.

name: Norjanah Antawan Sulaik
bio: Norjanah Antawan Sulaik is a textile designer based in Cotabato City, Mindanao, whose work adapts inaul weaving motifs into contemporary garments and interior fabrics. She studied industrial design in Davao City and later spent several years documenting abaca and pineapple-fiber dyeing methods practiced in upland and riverside communities.
